title: Personal Checking: small-item and small-balance overdraft fee exemptions by tier
content:
## Scope

Personal Checking has two de minimis amounts that keep small overdrafts free of fees. The per-item de minimis amount concerns the size of a single item; the end-of-day de minimis amount concerns how far the account's end-of-day ledger balance is negative on a business day.

## De minimis amounts by tier

| Tier | Per-item de minimis: items of this amount or less never incur an overdraft fee (USD) | End-of-day de minimis: no overdraft or returned-item fee for a business day whose end-of-day ledger balance is negative by this amount or less (USD) |
|---|---|---|
| Access Checking | 0.00 | 0.00 |
| Student Checking | 5.00 | 50.00 |
| Everyday Checking | 5.00 | 50.00 |
| Interest Checking | 5.00 | 50.00 |
| Premier Checking | 5.00 | 100.00 |
| Private Client Checking | 5.00 | 100.00 |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical amounts, derived from the table)

| Hypothetical situation on an Interest Checking account | Reading |
|---|---|
| An item of exactly 5.00 USD is paid into overdraft | The item is at the per-item de minimis amount, so it never incurs an overdraft fee |
| An item of 5.01 USD is paid into overdraft | The item is above the per-item de minimis amount |
| The end-of-day ledger balance is negative by exactly 50.00 USD | Within the end-of-day de minimis amount: no overdraft or returned-item fee for that business day |
| The end-of-day ledger balance is negative by 50.01 USD | Beyond the end-of-day de minimis amount |

**Q: Which tiers have the larger end-of-day amount?**
A: Premier Checking and Private Client Checking, at 100.00 USD; Student, Everyday and Interest Checking are at 50.00 USD.

**Q: Does "or less" include the exact amount?**
A: Yes. Both columns are stated as "this amount or less", so an item or a negative balance equal to the figure is inside the exemption.
